  | .inr .dread => .call 0 .whole [10] (.inr (.dcopy true)) (.inr (.dcopy false))
  | .inr (.dcopy b) => .jeq 14 13 (.inr (.dclear b)) (.inr (.dbump b))
  | .inr (.dbump b) => .inc 14 (.inr (.dcopy b))
  | .inr (.dclear b) => .clr 13 (.inr (.dscale b))
  | .inr (.dscale b) => .jz 14 (.inr (.dadd b)) (.inr (.dtake b))
  | .inr (.dtake b) => .dec 14 (.inr (.dinc b false))
  | .inr (.dinc b false) => .inc 13 (.inr (.dinc b true))
  | .inr (.dinc b true) => .inc 13 (.inr (.dscale b))
  | .inr (.dadd b) => if b then .inc 13 (.inr .dtest) else .jz 14 (.inr .dtest) (.inr .dtest)
  | .inr .q1T => .jeq 17 2 (.inr .q1d) (.inr .q1B)
  | .inr .q1B => .inc 17 (.inr .q1T)
  | .inr .q1d => .dec 17 (.inr .qsT)
  | .inr .qsT => .jz 17 (.inr .seek) (.inr .qsD)
  | .inr .qsD => .dec 17 (.inr (.qsI 0))
  | .inr (.qsI i) => .inc 16 (if i = 3 then .inr .qsT else .inr (.qsI (i + 1)))
  | .inr .seek => .jeq 15 16 (.inr .no) (.inr .probe)
  | .inr .probe => .jeq 17 13 (.inr .hit) (.inr .bump)
  | .inr .bump => .inc 17 (.inr (.sadv 0))
  | .inr (.sadv i) => .inc 15 (if i = 3 then .inr .seek else .inr (.sadv (i + 1)))
  | .inr .hit => if mode then .call 0 .whole [15] (.inr .yes) (.inr .no) else .ret true
  | .inr .yes => .ret true
  | .inr .no => .ret false

/-- **The bank's last phase.** From `q1T`, with `na + 1` in register `2`, the index `i` in
register `13` and the seek registers `15`, `16`, `17` clear, the bank answers: in mode `false`
whether `i < na`; in mode `true` letter `4i` of the input if `i < na`, and `0` otherwise.

**Proof sketch.** `registerCopy_loop` and one decrement load `na` into register `17`;
`registerScale_loop` at factor `4` moves `4 na` into the seek limit `16`; `indexedSeek_loop` at
stride `4` hits exactly when `i < na`, with its pointer at `4i`. -/
private theorem epad_bank_post (C d : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (z : List Bool) (B na i : ℕ)
    (v : Fin 18 → ℕ) (hv : ∀ r, v r ≤ B) (h2 : v 2 = na + 1) (h13 : v 13 = i)
    (h15 : v 15 = 0) (h16 : v 16 = 0) (h17 : v 17 = 0) (hB : 4 * na + 1 ≤ B) :
    AHalt (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .q1T), v, none)
      (if i < na then (if mode then z.getD (4 * i) false else true) else false) := by
  -- `17 := na + 1`, then `na`
  have hc1 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 17 2 (by decide) (.inr .q1T)
    (.inr .q1B) (.inr .q1d) rfl rfl B v hv (by rw [h17]; exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₁, hv₁⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update v 17 (v 2) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₁] at hc1
  have b₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₁]; exact register_update_le v 17 B _ hv (hv 2)
  obtain ⟨v₂, hv₂⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update v₁ 17 na := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have b₂ : ∀ r, v₂ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₂]; exact register_update_le v₁ 17 B _ b₁ (by omega)
  have hd : AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .q1d), v₁, none)
      (some (.inr .qsT), v₂, none) := by
    have hc : epadBA C d mode (.inr .q1d) = .dec 17 (.inr .qsT) := rfl
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc trivial, b₁⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_dec hc, hv₂, hv₁, Function.update_self, h2, Nat.add_sub_cancel,
      Function.update_idem]
    exact AReach.refl _
  -- `16 += 4 · 17`, `17 := 0`
  have hsc := registerScale_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 17 16 (by decide) (.inr .qsT)
    (.inr .qsD) (.inr .seek) (fun i => if h : i < 4 then .inr (.qsI ⟨i, h⟩) else .inr .qsT) 4
    rfl rfl (fun i hi => by
      obtain rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl : i = 0 ∨ i = 1 ∨ i = 2 ∨ i = 3 := by omega
      all_goals rfl) rfl B v₂ b₂ (by
        rw [hv₂, Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₁,
          Function.update_of_ne (by decide), h16]
        omega)
  obtain ⟨v₃, hv₃⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (Function.update v₂ 17 0) 16
      (v₂ 16 + 4 * v₂ 17) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₃] at hsc
  have h₃ : ∀ r, v₃ r = if r = 16 then 4 * na else if r = 17 then 0 else v r := by
    intro r
    rw [hv₃, hv₂, hv₁]
    simp only [Function.update_apply, Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h16]
    split_ifs <;> subst_vars <;> simp_all
  have b₃ : ∀ r, v₃ r ≤ B := by
    intro r; rw [h₃]; split_ifs
    · omega
    · exact Nat.zero_le _
    · exact hv r
  -- the seek
  have hseek := indexedSeek_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 15 16 17 13 (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.inr .seek) (.inr .probe) (.inr .bump)
    (.inr .hit) (.inr .no) (fun i => if h : i < 4 then .inr (.sadv ⟨i, h⟩) else .inr .seek) 4 B
    (by omega) rfl rfl rfl (fun i hi => by
      obtain rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl : i = 0 ∨ i = 1 ∨ i = 2 ∨ i = 3 := by omega
      all_goals rfl) rfl na v₃ b₃
    (by rw [h₃, h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h15]; omega)
    (by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; omega)
    (by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; exact Nat.zero_le _)
  have h313 : v₃ 13 = i := by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h13]
  have h317 : v₃ 17 = 0 := by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  have h315 : v₃ 15 = 0 := by rw [h₃]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, h15]
  rw [h313, h317, Nat.zero_add] at hseek
  refine hc1.halt (hd.halt (hsc.halt ?_))
  by_cases hi : i < na
  · rw [if_pos hi] at hseek ⊢
    obtain ⟨v₄, hv₄⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (Function.update v₃ 15 (v₃ 15 + 4 * (i - 0)))
        17 i := ⟨_, rfl⟩
    rw [← hv₄] at hseek
    have b₄ : ∀ r, v₄ r ≤ B := by
      rw [hv₄]
      refine register_update_le _ 17 B _ (register_update_le _ 15 B _ b₃ ?_) (by omega)
      rw [h315]; omega
    have h415 : v₄ 15 = 4 * i := by
      rw [hv₄, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), Function.update_self, h315]; omega
    refine hseek.halt ?_
    cases mode with
    | false =>
      exact AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d false (.inr .hit) = .ret true from rfl)
        trivial, b₄⟩
    | true =>
      have hc : epadBA C d true (.inr .hit) = .call 0 .whole [15] (.inr .yes) (.inr .no) := rfl
      refine AHalt.step ⟨epad_preS hc (List.nodup_singleton _), b₄⟩ ?_
      rw [astep_call hc, vword_whole₁, h415]
      have ho : epadOr 0 (pairEncode z (Nat.bits (4 * i))) = z.getD (4 * i) false :=
        (epadIn_answer z (4 * i)).1
      rw [ho]
      cases hb : z.getD (4 * i) false
      · exact AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d true (.inr .no) = .ret false from rfl)
          trivial, b₄⟩
      · exact AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d true (.inr .yes) = .ret true from rfl)
          trivial, b₄⟩
  · rw [if_neg hi] at hseek ⊢
    obtain ⟨v₄, hv₄⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (Function.update v₃ 15 (v₃ 16)) 17 na :=
      ⟨_, rfl⟩
    rw [← hv₄] at hseek
    have b₄ : ∀ r, v₄ r ≤ B := by
      rw [hv₄]
      exact register_update_le _ 17 B _ (register_update_le _ 15 B _ b₃ (b₃ 16)) (by omega)
    exact hseek.halt (AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS
      (show epadBA C d mode (.inr .no) = .ret false from rfl) trivial, b₄⟩)

/-- **The bank's first phase.** From the start, the bank counts `|z|` and parses
`z = ⟨y, w⟩`; it rejects a word that is not a pair, or whose index word `w` is not canonical
or wider than `|y|`; otherwise it decodes `i = bitsVal w` into register `13` and enters the
validity block with its pointer `0`, its limit `2 |y|` and its working registers clear, the
seek registers `15`–`17` clear, all registers at most `B`.

**Proof sketch.** `inputLength_loop`; `alignedPair_loop` at stride `1` on `z`; three
`registerCopy_loop`s, two decrements and a halving set the tail base `2|y| + 2`, the block's
limit `2|y|` and the cap `|y|`; `canonicalTail_loop` checks the index word; one more copy moves
the pointer to the end, and `boundedDecode_loop` decodes the index (its values stay below
`2 ^ |bits |y||` by `LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow`). -/
private theorem epad_bank_pre (C d : ℕ) (mode : Bool) (z : List Bool) (B : ℕ)
    (hB : 2 * z.length + 1 ≤ B) :
    (pairDecode z = none → ∃ v, (∀ r, v r ≤ B) ∧
      AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B)
        (some (.inr .lscan), fun _ => 0, none) (some (.inr .no), v, none)) ∧
    (∀ y w, pairDecode z = some (y, w) →
      (¬ (w.getLastD true = true ∧ w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length) → ∃ v, (∀ r, v r ≤ B) ∧
        AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
          (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B)
          (some (.inr .lscan), fun _ => 0, none) (some (.inr .no), v, none)) ∧
      (w.getLastD true = true ∧ w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length → ∃ v, (∀ r, v r ≤ B) ∧
        v 0 = 0 ∧ v 1 = 2 * y.length ∧ (∀ r : Fin 18, 2 ≤ r.val → r.val ≤ 8 → v r = 0) ∧
        v 13 = LogProg.bitsVal w ∧ v 15 = 0 ∧ v 16 = 0 ∧ v 17 = 0 ∧
        AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
          (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B)
          (some (.inr .lscan), fun _ => 0, none) (some (.inl .scan), v, none))) := by
  -- the length
  have hlen := inputLength_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 9 1 (.inr .lscan) (.inr .linc)
    (.inr .zscan) rfl rfl (fun n _ => (epadIn_answer z n).2) B (by omega) (fun _ => 0)
    (fun _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₀, hv₀⟩ : ∃ w, w = Function.update (fun _ : Fin 18 => 0) 9 z.length := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₀] at hlen
  have b₀ : ∀ r, v₀ r ≤ B := by
    rw [hv₀]; exact register_update_le _ 9 B _ (fun _ => Nat.zero_le _) (by omega)
  have h₀ : ∀ r : Fin 18, r ≠ 9 → v₀ r = 0 := fun r hr => by
    rw [hv₀, Function.update_of_ne hr]
  have h₀9 : v₀ 9 = z.length := by rw [hv₀, Function.update_self]
  -- the outer pair scan
  have hap := alignedPair_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 9 0 (.inr .zscan) (.inr .zfirst)
    (fun b => .inr (.ztest b)) (fun b => .inr (.zread b)) (.inr .no) (.inr .c1T)
    (fun k i => if i = 0 then .inr (.zadv k) else .inr (epadZEnd k)) 1 B (by omega) (by decide)
    rfl rfl (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun k i hi => by obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
                      rfl)
    ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩ z v₀ b₀ (by rw [h₀9, h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega)
    (fun i _ => by rw [h₀ 10 (by decide), Nat.zero_add, Nat.one_mul]
                   exact (epadIn_answer z i).1)
  refine ⟨fun hd => ?_, fun y w hd => ?_⟩
  · simp only [hd] at hap
    obtain ⟨t, ht, hr⟩ := hap
    exact ⟨_, register_update_le v₀ 10 B _ b₀ (by rw [h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega), hlen.trans hr⟩
  simp only [hd] at hap
  have hz : z = pairEncode y w := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z y w hd
  have hzl : z.length = 2 * y.length + 2 + w.length := by rw [hz, length_pairEncode]
  obtain ⟨v₁, hv₁⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₀ 10 (v₀ 10 + 1 * (2 * y.length + 2)) :=
    ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₁] at hap
  have b₁ : ∀ r, v₁ r ≤ B := by
    rw [hv₁]; exact register_update_le v₀ 10 B _ b₀ (by rw [h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega)
  have h₁10 : v₁ 10 = 2 * y.length + 2 := by
    rw [hv₁, Function.update_self, h₀ 10 (by decide)]; omega
  -- the tail base, the block's limit and the cap
  have hc1 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 11 10 (by decide) (.inr .c1T)
    (.inr .c1B) (.inr .c2T) rfl rfl B v₁ b₁ (by
      rw [hv₁, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), h₀ 11 (by decide)]; exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₂, hv₂⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₁ 11 (v₁ 10) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₂] at hc1
  have b₂ : ∀ r, v₂ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₂]; exact register_update_le v₁ 11 B _ b₁ (b₁ 10)
  have hc2 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 1 10 (by decide) (.inr .c2T)
    (.inr .c2B) (.inr .dd1) rfl rfl B v₂ b₂ (by
      rw [hv₂, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₁, Function.update_of_ne (by decide),
        h₀ 1 (by decide)]
      exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₃, hv₃⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₂ 1 (v₂ 10) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₃] at hc2
  have b₃ : ∀ r, v₃ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₃]; exact register_update_le v₂ 1 B _ b₂ (b₂ 10)
  have h₂10 : v₂ 10 = 2 * y.length + 2 := by
    rw [hv₂, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), h₁10]
  obtain ⟨v₄, hv₄⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₃ 1 (2 * y.length) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have b₄ : ∀ r, v₄ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₄]; exact register_update_le v₃ 1 B _ b₃ (by omega)
  have hdd : AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .dd1), v₃, none)
      (some (.inr .c3T), v₄, none) := by
    have hc : epadBA C d mode (.inr .dd1) = .dec 1 (.inr .dd2) := rfl
    have hc' : epadBA C d mode (.inr .dd2) = .dec 1 (.inr .c3T) := rfl
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc trivial, b₃⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_dec hc]
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc' trivial,
      register_update_le v₃ 1 B _ b₃ ((Nat.sub_le _ _).trans (b₃ 1))⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_dec hc']
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v₃ 1 (v₃ 1 - 1)) 1
        (Function.update v₃ 1 (v₃ 1 - 1) 1 - 1) = v₄ := by
      rw [hv₄, hv₃]
      funext s
      simp only [Function.update_apply]
      split_ifs <;> simp_all
    rw [e]
    exact AReach.refl _
  have hc3 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 12 1 (by decide) (.inr .c3T)
    (.inr .c3B) (.inr .hcap) rfl rfl B v₄ b₄ (by
      rw [hv₄, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₃, Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₂,
        Function.update_of_ne (by decide), hv₁, Function.update_of_ne (by decide),
        h₀ 12 (by decide)]
      exact Nat.zero_le _)
  obtain ⟨v₅, hv₅⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₄ 12 (v₄ 1) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₅] at hc3
  have b₅ : ∀ r, v₅ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₅]; exact register_update_le v₄ 12 B _ b₄ (b₄ 1)
  obtain ⟨v₆, hv₆⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v₅ 12 y.length := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have b₆ : ∀ r, v₆ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₆]; exact register_update_le v₅ 12 B _ b₅ (by omega)
  have hhc : AReach (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z
      (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) (some (.inr .hcap), v₅, none)
      (some (.inr (.ttest true)), v₆, none) := by
    have hc : epadBA C d mode (.inr .hcap) = .half 12 (.inr (.ttest true)) := rfl
    refine AReach.step ⟨epad_preS hc trivial, b₅⟩ ?_
    rw [astep_half hc]
    have e : Function.update v₅ 12 (v₅ 12 / 2) = v₆ := by
      rw [hv₆, hv₅]
      funext s
      simp only [Function.update_apply]
      split_ifs <;> simp_all
    rw [e]
    exact AReach.refl _
  -- the register file before the tail check
  have h₆ : ∀ r : Fin 18, v₆ r = if r = 1 then 2 * y.length else if r = 9 then z.length
      else if r = 10 then 2 * y.length + 2 else if r = 11 then 2 * y.length + 2
      else if r = 12 then y.length else 0 := by
    intro r
    rw [hv₆, hv₅, hv₄, hv₃, hv₂, hv₁, hv₀]
    simp only [Function.update_apply, Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
    split_ifs <;> simp_all
  -- the tail check
  have hct := canonicalTail_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 9 12 (by decide) (by decide)
    (by decide) 0 (fun b => .inr (.ttest b)) (.inr .tcheck) (.inr .tread) (.inr .no) (.inr .c4T)
    (fun b => .inr (.thalve b)) (fun b i => if i = 0 then .inr (.tadv b) else .inr (.ttest b))
    1 B (by omega) (fun _ => rfl) rfl rfl (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun b i hi => by obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
                      rfl)
    (fun _ => rfl) w true v₆ b₆ (by rw [h₆, h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; omega)
    (fun i hi => by
      rw [h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte, Nat.one_mul]
      rw [(epadIn_answer z _).1, hz, pairEncode_getD_snd])
  obtain ⟨v', b', hp', hfr', hct⟩ := hct
  have h612 : v₆ 12 = y.length := by rw [h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  rw [h612] at hct
  refine ⟨fun hbad => ?_, fun hok => ?_⟩
  · have hno : (if w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length then
        (if w.getLastD true = true then (Sum.inr EPadBX.c4T : EPadVL C d ⊕ EPadBX)
          else .inr .no) else .inr .no) = .inr .no := by
      split_ifs with h1 h2
      · exact absurd ⟨h2, h1⟩ hbad
      · rfl
      · rfl
    rw [hno] at hct
    exact ⟨v', b', hlen.trans (hap.trans (hc1.trans (hc2.trans (hdd.trans (hc3.trans
      (hhc.trans hct))))))⟩
  rw [if_pos hok.2, if_pos hok.1] at hct
  -- the pointer to the end, then the decoder
  have h'9 : v' 9 = z.length := by
    rw [hfr' 9 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  have hc4 := registerCopy_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 9 (by decide) (.inr .c4T)
    (.inr .c4B) (.inr .dtest) rfl rfl B v' b' (by
      rw [h'9]; rw [h₆] at hp'; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte] at hp'; exact hp')
  obtain ⟨v₇, hv₇⟩ : ∃ u, u = Function.update v' 10 (v' 9) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  rw [← hv₇] at hc4
  have b₇ : ∀ r, v₇ r ≤ B := by rw [hv₇]; exact register_update_le v' 10 B _ b' (b' 9)
  have h₇ : ∀ r : Fin 18, r ≠ 10 → r ≠ 12 → v₇ r = v₆ r := fun r h10 h12 => by
    rw [hv₇, Function.update_of_ne h10, hfr' r h10 h12]
  have hw : w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length := hok.2
  have hval : ∀ i ≤ w.length, LogProg.bitsVal (w.drop i) ≤ B := by
    intro i _
    have h1 := LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow (w.drop i)
    have h2 : 2 ^ (w.drop i).length ≤ 2 ^ (Nat.bits y.length).length :=
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) ((by simp : (w.drop i).length ≤ w.length).trans hw)
    by_cases hy0 : y.length = 0
    · rw [hy0, Nat.zero_bits, List.length_nil, pow_zero] at h2
      omega
    · have h3 := LogProg.two_pow_bits_le y.length (by omega)
      omega
  have hdec := boundedDecode_loop (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z 10 11 13 14 (by decide)
    (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) 0 (.inr .dtest) (.inr .ddown)
    (.inr .dread) (.inl .scan) (fun b => .inr (.dcopy b)) (fun b => .inr (.dbump b))
    (fun b => .inr (.dclear b)) (fun b => .inr (.dscale b)) (fun b => .inr (.dtake b))
    (fun b => .inr (.dadd b))
    (fun b i => if i = 0 then .inr (.dinc b false) else if i = 1 then .inr (.dinc b true)
      else .inr (.dscale b))
    rfl rfl rfl (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl)
    (fun b i hi => by
      obtain rfl | rfl : i = 0 ∨ i = 1 := by omega
      all_goals rfl)
    (fun _ => rfl) (fun b => by cases b <;> rfl) w B hval w.length le_rfl v₇ b₇
    (by rw [hv₇, Function.update_self, h'9, Function.update_of_ne (by decide),
          hfr' 11 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
        simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]; omega)
    (by rw [h₇ 13 (by decide) (by decide), h₆, List.drop_length]
        simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
        rw [← Nat.zero_bits, LogProg.bitsVal_bits])
    (by rw [h₇ 14 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte])
    (fun i hi => by
      rw [h₇ 11 (by decide) (by decide), h₆]; simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
      rw [(epadIn_answer z _).1, hz, pairEncode_getD_snd])
  obtain ⟨v'', b'', -, h''13, -, hfr'', hdec⟩ := hdec
  have h'' : ∀ r : Fin 18, r ≠ 10 → r ≠ 12 → r ≠ 13 → r ≠ 14 → v'' r = v₆ r :=
    fun r h10 h12 h13 h14 => by rw [hfr'' r h10 h13 h14, h₇ r h10 h12]
  refine ⟨v'', b'', ?_, ?_, fun r h2 h8 => ?_, h''13, ?_, ?_, ?_, hlen.trans (hap.trans
    (hc1.trans (hc2.trans (hdd.trans (hc3.trans (hhc.trans (hct.trans (hc4.trans hdec))))))))⟩
  · rw [h'' 0 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  · rw [h'' 1 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [↓reduceIte]
  · have hne : ∀ k : Fin 18, 9 ≤ k.val → r ≠ k := fun k hk h => by rw [h] at h8; omega
    have hne1 : r ≠ 1 := fun h => by rw [h] at h2; simp at h2
    rw [h'' r (hne 10 (by decide)) (hne 12 (by decide)) (hne 13 (by decide))
      (hne 14 (by decide)), h₆, if_neg hne1, if_neg (hne 9 (by decide)),
      if_neg (hne 10 (by decide)), if_neg (hne 11 (by decide)), if_neg (hne 12 (by decide))]
  · rw [h'' 15 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  · rw [h'' 16 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]
  · rw [h'' 17 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), h₆]
    simp only [Fin.reduceEq, ↓reduceIte]

/-- Letter `4i` of `⟨⟨a, b⟩, w⟩` is letter `i` of `a`, for `i < |a|`. -/
private lemma epad_getD_four (a b w : List Bool) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < a.length) :
    (pairEncode (pairEncode a b) w).getD (4 * i) false = a.getD i false := by
  rw [pairEncode_getD, if_pos (by rw [length_pairEncode]; omega),
    show 4 * i / 2 = 2 * i by omega, pairEncode_getD, if_pos (by omega),
    show 2 * i / 2 = i by omega]

/-- **The bank**: both query languages are decided in logarithmic space.

**Proof sketch.** `arm_decides_poly` on `epadBA`: the first phase `epad_bank_pre` parses the
query and decodes its index (rejecting malformed queries), the validity block `epad_val_run`
runs at stride `2` on the first field (rejecting unpadded words), and `epad_bank_post` answers.
Registers stay below `(C + d + 8)(|z| + 1)^{d + 1}`. -/
private theorem epad_Q_mem (C d : ℕ) (mode : Bool) : epadQ C d mode ∈ LOGSPACE := by
  classical
  letI := epadVLFintype C d
  letI := epadBXFintype
  refine arm_decides_poly (epadBA C d mode) (.inr .lscan) epadIn epadIn_mem (C + d + 8) (d + 1)
    fun z => ?_
  have hB := epad_bound C d z.length
  obtain ⟨hnone, hsome⟩ := epad_bank_pre C d mode z ((C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1))
    (by omega)
  have hno : ∀ v : Fin 18 → ℕ, (∀ r, v r ≤ (C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1)) →
      AHalt (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z (fun a => PreS (epadBA C d mode) z a ∧
        ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ (C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1)) (some (.inr .no), v, none)
        false := fun v hv =>
    AHalt.ret rfl ⟨epad_preS (show epadBA C d mode (.inr .no) = .ret false from rfl) trivial, hv⟩
  cases hd : pairDecode z with
  | none =>
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hr⟩ := hnone hd
    have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z = false := by
      rw [indicator_eq_decide]; exact decide_eq_false (epad_not_mem_Q hd)
    rw [hans]
    exact hr.halt (hno v hv)
  | some yw =>
    obtain ⟨y, w⟩ := yw
    obtain ⟨hbad, hok⟩ := hsome y w hd
    have hz : z = pairEncode y w := eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode z y w hd
    have hzl : z.length = 2 * y.length + 2 + w.length := by rw [hz, length_pairEncode]
    by_cases hw : w.getLastD true = true ∧ w.length ≤ (Nat.bits y.length).length
    · obtain ⟨v, hv, h0, h1, hzr, h13, h15, h16, h17, hr⟩ := hok hw
      have hpowy : C * (y.length + 1) ^ d ≤ C * (z.length + 1) ^ d :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) _)
      obtain ⟨v', hfr, hb', hval2, hr'⟩ := epad_val_run (epadBA C d mode) epadOr z y true C d
        Sum.inl (.inr .q1T) (.inr .no) (fun _ => rfl)
        (fun j hj => by
          rw [show epadS true * j = 2 * j from rfl, (epadIn_answer z _).1, hz, pairEncode_getD,
            if_pos (by omega), show 2 * j / 2 = j by omega])
        ((C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1)) (by omega) v hv h0 h1 hzr
      by_cases hvy : epadValid C d y
      · rw [if_pos hvy] at hr'
        obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hvy
        have hfst : pairFstD y = a := by rw [ha, pairFstD_pairEncode]
        have hya : y.length = 2 * a.length + 2 + C * (a.length + 1) ^ d := by
          rw [ha, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
        have hpost := epad_bank_post C d mode z ((C + d + 8) * (z.length + 1) ^ (d + 1))
          a.length (LogProg.bitsVal w) v' hb' (by rw [hval2 ⟨a, ha⟩, hfst])
          (by rw [hfr 13 (by decide), h13]) (by rw [hfr 15 (by decide), h15])
          (by rw [hfr 16 (by decide), h16]) (by rw [hfr 17 (by decide), h17]) (by omega)
        have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z =
            (if LogProg.bitsVal w < a.length then
              (if mode then z.getD (4 * LogProg.bitsVal w) false else true) else false) := by
          rw [indicator_eq_decide]
          have hm := epad_mem_Q_iff (C := C) (d := d) (mode := mode) hd
          rw [hfst] at hm
          by_cases hi : LogProg.bitsVal w < a.length
          · rw [if_pos hi]
            cases mode with
            | false =>
              exact decide_eq_true (hm.mpr ⟨hw.1, hw.2, ⟨a, ha⟩, by simpa using hi⟩)
            | true =>
              have h4 : z.getD (4 * LogProg.bitsVal w) false = a.getD (LogProg.bitsVal w) false :=
                by rw [hz, ha, epad_getD_four a _ w _ hi]
              rw [if_pos rfl, h4]
              cases hb : a.getD (LogProg.bitsVal w) false
              · refine decide_eq_false (fun h => ?_)
                have h5 := (hm.mp h).2.2.2
                rw [if_pos rfl, hb] at h5
                exact Bool.false_ne_true h5
              · exact decide_eq_true (hm.mpr ⟨hw.1, hw.2, ⟨a, ha⟩, by rw [if_pos rfl]; exact hb⟩)
          · rw [if_neg hi]
            refine decide_eq_false (fun h => ?_)
            have h4 := (hm.mp h).2.2.2
            cases mode with
            | false => exact hi (by simpa using h4)
            | true =>
              simp only [if_true] at h4
              rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega),
                Option.getD_none] at h4
              exact Bool.false_ne_true h4
        rw [hans]
        exact hr.halt (hr'.halt hpost)
      · rw [if_neg hvy] at hr'
        have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z = false := by
          rw [indicator_eq_decide]
          exact decide_eq_false (fun h => hvy ((epad_mem_Q_iff hd).mp h).2.2.1)
        rw [hans]
        exact hr.halt (hr'.halt (hno v' hb'))
    · obtain ⟨v, hv, hr⟩ := hbad hw
      have hans : MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadQ C d mode : Set (List Bool)) z = false := by
        rw [indicator_eq_decide]
        exact decide_eq_false (fun h => hw ⟨((epad_mem_Q_iff hd).mp h).1,
          ((epad_mem_Q_iff hd).mp h).2.1⟩)
      rw [hans]
      exact hr.halt (hno v hv)

/-! ### The run phase -/

/-- **The run phase**: the oracle-input simulator runs `L`'s decider on the
virtual input `epadVirt y`, answered by the bank, within `K · T |y|` work cells, on every input.

**Proof sketch.** `LogProg.OIS.compile_decides` with `L`'s decider `M` (space `c · S`) and the
bank `![M₀, M₁]` of `epadQ`'s deciders (space `c_j · logSpace`), whose laws on genuine queries
are `epad_query_mem_iff`. With `m = |y|` and `v = epadVirt y`: on a padded `y = ⟨a, 1^{…}⟩`,
`m = 2|a| + 2 + C (|a| + 1)^d`, so `S |v| ≤ T m` by `hST`; otherwise `v = []` and
`S 0 ≤ S 0 · T m`. The index register costs `|bits (|v| + 1)| + 2 ≤ 4 T m` and the bank
`k_D (2B + 1)` with `B = (c₀ + c₁)(3m + 4) + 1`, so `2B + 1 ≤ (8 (c₀ + c₁) + 3) T m`. -/
private theorem epad_run {L : Language Bool} {S T : ℕ → ℕ} (C d : ℕ) (hL : L ∈ SPACE S)
    (hST : ∀ n, S n ≤ T (2 * n + 2 + C * (n + 1) ^ d)) (hT : ∀ m, m + 1 ≤ T m) :
    ∃ (K : ℕ) (O : FinTM Bool), O.ComputesInSpace
      (fun y => [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) (epadVirt C d y)])
      (fun n => K * T n) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨c, M, hM⟩ := mem_SPACE_iff.mp hL
  have hQ0 := epad_Q_mem C d false
  have hQ1 := epad_Q_mem C d true
  rw [LOGSPACE_eq, mem_SPACE_iff] at hQ0 hQ1
  obtain ⟨c0, M0, h0⟩ := hQ0
  obtain ⟨c1, M1, h1⟩ := hQ1
  let Ms : Fin 2 → FinTM Bool := ![M0, M1]
  let As : Fin 2 → Language Bool := ![epadQ C d false, epadQ C d true]
  let sb : Fin 2 → ℕ → ℕ := ![fun n => c0 * logSpace n, fun n => c1 * logSpace n]
  have hMs : ∀ j, (Ms j).DecidesInSpace (As j) (sb j) := by
    intro j
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => Fin.elim0 i)) j
    · show M0.DecidesInSpace (epadQ C d false) (fun n => c0 * logSpace n)
      exact h0
    · show M1.DecidesInSpace (epadQ C d true) (fun n => c1 * logSpace n)
      exact h1
  have hsb : ∀ j q, sb j q ≤ (c0 + c1) * (q + 1) := by
    intro j q
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => Fin.elim0 i)) j
    · show c0 * logSpace q ≤ (c0 + c1) * (q + 1)
      exact Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.le_add_right _ _) (logSpace_le_succ q)
    · show c1 * logSpace q ≤ (c0 + c1) * (q + 1)
      exact Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.le_add_left _ _) (logSpace_le_succ q)
  refine ⟨M.k * (2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) + 4 +
      (LogProg.bankK Ms + LogProg.bankK Ms) * (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3),
    LogProg.compileFinTM (LogProg.OIS.prog M) (LogProg.OIS.start M) (LogProg.bankTM Ms)
      (LogProg.bankStart Ms), ?_⟩
  rw [FinTM.computesInSpace_iff]
  intro y
  set v := epadVirt C d y with hv
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hs⟩ :=
    (FinTM.computesInSpace_iff _ _ _).mp ((FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff _ _ _).mp hM) v
  have hvm : v.length ≤ y.length := epadVirt_length_le C d y
  set B := (c0 + c1) * (3 * y.length + 4) + 1 with hB
  have hbits : ∀ i ≤ v.length, (Nat.bits i).length ≤ y.length + 1 := by
    intro i hi
    exact (Turing.length_bits_le_self i).trans ((hi.trans hvm).trans (Nat.le_succ _))
  have hBnd : ∀ j, ∀ i ≤ v.length,
      max (sb j (pairEncode y (Nat.bits i)).length) 1 ≤ B := by
    intro j i hi
    have hq := hsb j (pairEncode y (Nat.bits i)).length
    rw [length_pairEncode] at hq ⊢
    have hb := hbits i hi
    have hmono : (c0 + c1) * (2 * y.length + 2 + (Nat.bits i).length + 1) ≤
        (c0 + c1) * (3 * y.length + 4) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega)
    refine max_le ?_ (by omega)
    omega
  have hA0 : ∀ i ≤ v.length,
      pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ As 0 ↔ i < v.length := by
    intro i hi
    show pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ epadQ C d false ↔ i < v.length
    rw [epad_query_mem_iff C d false y i (hi.trans hvm)]
    simp only [Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_valid hval]
      exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hval, h⟩⟩
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_not_valid hval]
      exact ⟨fun h => absurd h.1 hval, fun h => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)⟩
  have hA1 : ∀ i < v.length,
      pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ As 1 ↔ v.getD i false = true := by
    intro i hi
    show pairEncode y (Nat.bits i) ∈ epadQ C d true ↔ v.getD i false = true
    rw [epad_query_mem_iff C d true y i (hi.le.trans hvm)]
    simp only [if_true]
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_valid hval]
      exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hval, h⟩⟩
    · rw [hv, epadVirt_of_not_valid hval] at hi
      exact absurd hi (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  obtain ⟨T', hT', hSp⟩ := LogProg.OIS.compile_decides M Ms As sb hMs y v
    [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) v] hA0 hA1 t ht B hBnd
  refine ⟨T', hT', hSp.trans ?_⟩
  -- the space ledger
  have hTm := hT y.length
  have hS : S v.length ≤ (S 0 + 1) * T y.length := by
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hval
      have hva : v.length = a.length := by
        rw [hv, epadVirt_of_valid ⟨a, ha⟩, ha, pairFstD_pairEncode]
      have hma : y.length = 2 * a.length + 2 + C * (a.length + 1) ^ d := by
        rw [ha, length_pairEncode, List.length_replicate]
      rw [hva]
      have h1 := hST a.length
      rw [← hma] at h1
      calc S a.length ≤ T y.length := h1
        _ ≤ (S 0 + 1) * T y.length := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_left _ (Nat.succ_pos _)
    · have hv0 : v.length = 0 := by rw [hv, epadVirt_of_not_valid hval]; rfl
      rw [hv0]
      calc S 0 ≤ S 0 * T y.length := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
        _ ≤ (S 0 + 1) * T y.length := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_succ _)
  have hsp : M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg v) t ≤ c * ((S 0 + 1) * T y.length) :=
    hs.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left c hS)
  have hW : (Nat.bits (v.length + 1)).length + 2 ≤ 4 * T y.length := by
    have h1 := Turing.length_bits_le_self (v.length + 1)
    omega
  have h2B : 2 * B + 1 ≤ (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length := by
    have h1 : (c0 + c1) * (3 * y.length + 4) ≤ (c0 + c1) * (4 * T y.length) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega)
    have e : (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length =
        2 * ((c0 + c1) * (4 * T y.length)) + 3 * T y.length := by ring
    rw [e, hB]
    omega
  have hk1 : M.k * (2 * M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg v) t + 1) ≤
      M.k * ((2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) * T y.length) := by
    apply Nat.mul_le_mul_left
    have e : (2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) * T y.length =
        2 * (c * ((S 0 + 1) * T y.length)) + T y.length := by ring
    rw [e]
    omega
  set kD := LogProg.bankK Ms + LogProg.bankK Ms with hkD
  have hk2 : kD * (2 * B + 1) ≤ kD * ((8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length) :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ h2B
  have e : (M.k * (2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) + 4 + kD * (8 * (c0 + c1) + 3)) * T y.length =
      M.k * ((2 * c * (S 0 + 1) + 1) * T y.length) + 4 * T y.length +
        kD * ((8 * (c0 + c1) + 3) * T y.length) := by ring
  rw [e]
  omega

/-- **Padding transfers space bounds down** ([AB09, Exercise 3.2], the padding argument in space
form): if `L ∈ SPACE S`, then the language of `L`'s members padded by `C · (|x| + 1)^d` ones lies
in `SPACE T` for every `T` with `m + 1 ≤ T m` (room to validate the padding and to copy the first
component) and `S n ≤ T (2n + 2 + C (n + 1)^d)` (room for `L`'s decider, at the padded length
`|pairEncode x 1^{C (|x|+1)^d}| = 2|x| + 2 + C (|x| + 1)^d`).

**Proof sketch.** Let `M` decide `L` within `c · S` cells. On input `y`, first check that `y` is a
pair `pairEncode x w` whose second component `w` consists of exactly `C (|x| + 1)^d` ones;
reject otherwise. That needs `O(log |y|) ⊆ O(|y| + 1)` cells, on malformed inputs too, and never
writes the pad. Then run `M` on `x`, read in place as a virtual input, and answer as `M` does,
within `c · S |x|` cells for `M` plus `O(|y| + 1)` for the simulation. For a validated `y`,
`|y| = 2|x| + 2 + C (|x| + 1)^d`, so `S |x| ≤ T |y|`, and both phases fit in `O(T |y|)`.

**Implementation.** Three machines and the catalog's conditional
(`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond_spaceUsed`): the validator decides the padded words in
logarithmic space (`epad_V_mem`, an abstract register machine through
`Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_poly`); on a padded word the run phase (`epad_run`) runs `M`
through the oracle-input simulator `Complexity.LogProg.OIS.compile_decides` on the virtual
input `epadVirt y` (the first component of a padded word, `[]` otherwise), whose length and bit
queries a bank of two logspace deciders answers (`epad_Q_mem`); otherwise the constant `[false]`
machine answers. The run phase's space is
`M.k (2 c S |v| + 1) + |bits (|v| + 1)| + 2 + k_D (2B + 1)` with `B = O(|y| + 1)`;
`S |v| ≤ (S 0 + 1) T |y|` both on padded words (by `hST`) and off them (`v = []`), and
`|y| + 1 ≤ T |y|` absorbs the rest. -/
theorem mem_SPACE_padLang {L : Language Bool} {S T : ℕ → ℕ} (C d : ℕ) (hL : L ∈ SPACE S)
    (hST : ∀ n, S n ≤ T (2 * n + 2 + C * (n + 1) ^ d)) (hT : ∀ m, m + 1 ≤ T m) :
    padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) ∈ SPACE T := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨K, O, hO⟩ := epad_run C d hL hST hT
  have hV := epad_V_mem C d
  rw [LOGSPACE_eq, mem_SPACE_iff] at hV
  obtain ⟨cV, D, hD⟩ := hV
  rw [FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff] at hD
  obtain ⟨hDt, hDs⟩ := hD.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le
  obtain ⟨hOt, hOs⟩ := hO.computesFunInTime_and_forall_spaceUsed_le
  obtain ⟨Mf, cf, hMf, hMfs⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_const_spaceUsed [false]
  obtain ⟨Mc, cc, hMc, hMcs⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond_spaceUsed
    (p := fun y => MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) y)
    (fun n => cV * logSpace n) (fun n => K * T n) (fun _ => cf) hDt hOt hMf hDs hOs hMfs
  rw [mem_SPACE_iff]
  refine ⟨cV + K + cf + cc, Mc, ?_⟩
  rw [FinTM.decidesInSpace_iff, FinTM.computesInSpace_iff]
  intro y
  have hout : (if MultiTapeTM.indicator (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) y = true then
      [MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) (epadVirt C d y)] else [false]) =
      [MultiTapeTM.indicator (padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) : Set (List Bool)) y] := by
    rw [LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, LogProg.indicator_eq_decide]
    by_cases hval : epadValid C d y
    · have hmem : y ∈ (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) := epad_mem_V.mpr hval
      rw [epadVirt_of_valid hval]
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hval
      have hpad : y ∈ (padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) : Set (List Bool)) ↔
          pairFstD y ∈ (L : Set (List Bool)) := by
        rw [ha, pairFstD_pairEncode]
        constructor
        · intro h
          obtain ⟨x, hx, hxe⟩ := mem_padLang_iff.mp h
          have := congrArg pairFstD hxe
          rw [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairFstD_pairEncode] at this
          rw [this]; exact hx
        · intro h
          exact mem_padLang_iff.mpr ⟨a, h, rfl⟩
      simp only [hmem, decide_true, if_true, List.cons.injEq, and_true]
      exact decide_eq_decide.mpr hpad.symm
    · have hmem : y ∉ (epadV C d : Set (List Bool)) := fun h => hval (epad_mem_V.mp h)
      have hpad : y ∉ (padLang L (fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ d) : Set (List Bool)) := by
        intro h
        obtain ⟨x, -, hxe⟩ := mem_padLang_iff.mp h
        exact hval ⟨x, hxe⟩
      simp only [hmem, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, hpad]
  have hc := (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mp hMc y
  rw [hout] at hc
  refine ⟨_, hc, (hMcs y _).trans ?_⟩
  have hTy := hT y.length
  have h1 : cV * logSpace y.length ≤ cV * T y.length :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ ((logSpace_le_succ _).trans hTy)
  have h2 : max (K * T y.length) cf ≤ K * T y.length + cf * T y.length :=
    max_le (Nat.le_add_right _ _) (le_add_left (Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)))
  have h3 : cc ≤ cc * T y.length := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
  have e : (cV + K + cf + cc) * T y.length =
      cV * T y.length + K * T y.length + cf * T y.length + cc * T y.length := by ring
  rw [e]
  omega

end Complexity

import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.Finset
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.Abs
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.Int
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Dedup
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Max

import Mathlib.Data.Sign.Defs

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Configurations of Multi-Tape Turing Machines

Configurations of a multi-tape Turing machine with a read-only input tape, `k` work tapes and one
write-only output tape, together with what a single transition does to one and the space measure
read off a list of them.

## Design

Nothing here mentions a machine. A step is described in two parts: an `Action`, recording
which way the input head moves, what is written and where the work heads move, which symbol is
emitted and which state follows; and `Action.apply`, which carries it out on a
configuration.

The output tape is part of the configuration, so the string emitted along a run can be read off
the configuration the run ends in.

## Main definitions

* `Cfg`: the configuration: the internal state, the tape contents and head positions, and the
    output tape
* `Action`: what a machine does in one step
* `Action.apply`: the effect of one action on a configuration
* `Cfg.Halted`, `Cfg.init`: halting, and the configuration a machine starts in
* `spaceUsedOfCfgs`: work tape cells touched along a list of configurations

**The specification API** (user, 2026-10-16): `Turing.Cfg.init_state`, `_inputPos`,
`_workTapes`, `_workTapePos` and `_output`, the initial configuration's fields as equations.
`Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol_of_zero`, `Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol_of_end` (with `inputSymbolInner`) and
`Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols_eq`: the heads' readings.

**The brief-inventory API, round 3** (user, 2026-10-17): `Turing.Action.apply_state`,
`_inputPos`, `_workTapePos` and `_output`, the applied action's fields as equations.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the k-tape Turing machine.)
* [Pap94] C. Papadimitriou, *Computational Complexity*, Addison-Wesley, 1994.
  (§2.3, §2.5: the machine model and the space measure.)
-/

namespace Turing

variable {k : ℕ} {State Symbol : Type*} {input : List Symbol}

/-- What a machine does in one step. -/
structure Action (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*) where
  /-- The movement (attempt) of the input head. -/
  inputTape : SignType
  /-- Actions on the work tapes: optionally a symbol to write and the head movement. -/
  workTapes : Fin k → (Option (Option Symbol)) × SignType
  /-- An optional symbol to output. -/
  output : Option Symbol
  /-- The successor state or none to halt. -/
  state : Option State

/--
The configurations of a Turing machine is relative to the input of the machine and consist of:
- an `Option`al state (or none for the halting state),
- the position of the input head (shifted by one),
- the contents of the work tape,
- the positions of the work tape heads,
- the contents of the write-only output tape
-/
@[ext]
structure Cfg (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*) (input : List Symbol) where
  /-- the state of the TM (or none for the halting state) -/
  state : Option State
  /-- the position of the input head, shifted by one -/
  inputPos : Fin (input.length + 2)
  /-- the work tapes -/
  workTapes : Fin k → ℤ → Option Symbol
  /-- the positions of the heads on the work tapes -/
  workTapePos : Fin k → ℤ
  /-- the contents of the write-only output tape -/
  output : List Symbol
deriving Inhabited

/-- Two configurations of a machine without work tapes are equal if their states, input head
positions and outputs are equal. -/
lemma Cfg.ext_zero_tapes {Symbol State : Type*} {input : List Symbol}
    {cfg₁ cfg₂ : Cfg 0 Symbol State input} (state : cfg₁.state = cfg₂.state)
    (inputPos : cfg₁.inputPos = cfg₂.inputPos) (output : cfg₁.output = cfg₂.output) :
    cfg₁ = cfg₂ :=
  Cfg.ext state inputPos (funext fun i => i.elim0) (funext fun i => i.elim0) output

/-- Attempt to move the input tape head.
The machine can only read one empty cell outside of the input,
any attempted movement beyond that results in no movement.

The addition is performed in `ℤ` before clamping. Performing it in `Fin (n + 2)` would wrap an
outward boundary move to the opposite end of the input. -/
@[scoped grind =]
def moveInputPos {n : ℕ} (pos : Fin (n + 2)) (m : SignType) : Fin (n + 2) :=
  let p := ((pos.val : ℤ) + (m.cast : ℤ)).toNat
  if h : p < n + 2 then ⟨p, h⟩ else ⟨n + 1, by omega⟩

@[simp]
lemma moveInputPos_zero {n : ℕ} (pos : Fin (n + 2)) :
    moveInputPos pos 0 = pos := by
  apply Fin.ext
  simp [moveInputPos, pos.isLt]

@[simp]
lemma moveInputPos_leftBoundary {n : ℕ} :
    moveInputPos (0 : Fin (n + 2)) (-1) = 0 := by
  apply Fin.ext
  simp [moveInputPos]

@[simp]
lemma moveInputPos_rightBoundary {n : ℕ} :
    moveInputPos (⟨n + 1, by omega⟩ : Fin (n + 2)) 1 = ⟨n + 1, by omega⟩ := by
  -- ported proof: `dite_eq_right` does not exist at our mathlib pin
  apply Fin.ext
  simp only [moveInputPos, SignType.coe_one]
  split <;> simp <;> omega

/-- A left move away from the left input boundary decrements the native input position. -/
lemma moveInputPos_neg_of_ne_left {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 2)) (h : p ≠ 0) :
    moveInputPos p .neg = ⟨p.val - 1, by have := p.isLt; omega⟩ := by
  -- ported proof: `dite_eq_left` does not exist at our mathlib pin
  have hlt := p.isLt
  apply Fin.ext
  simp only [moveInputPos, SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, SignType.coe_neg_one]
  split <;> simp <;> omega

/-- A right move away from the right input boundary increments the native input position. -/
lemma moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 2)) (h : p.val ≠ n + 1) :
    moveInputPos p .pos = ⟨p.val + 1, by have := p.isLt; omega⟩ := by
  -- ported proof: `dite_eq_left` does not exist at our mathlib pin
  have hlt := p.isLt
  apply Fin.ext
  simp only [moveInputPos, SignType.pos_eq_one, SignType.coe_one]
  split <;> simp <;> omega

/-- The symbol currently under the input tape head. -/
def Cfg.inputSymbol (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Option Symbol :=
  if h₁ : cfg.inputPos = 0 then none
  else if h₂ : cfg.inputPos = input.length + 1 then none
  else input[cfg.inputPos.val - 1]'(by
    -- ported proof: `grind` at our pin does not bridge the `Fin` equality with `.val`
    have h0 : (cfg.inputPos : ℕ) ≠ 0 := fun hv => h₁ (Fin.val_eq_zero_iff.mp hv)
    have hlt := cfg.inputPos.isLt
    omega)

@[simp]
lemma inputSymbolInner {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (p : ℕ)
    (h₁ : cfg.inputPos.val = 1 + p)
    (h₂ : p < input.length) :
    cfg.inputSymbol = some input[p] := by
  -- ported proof: `grind` at our pin does not bridge the `Fin` equality with `.val`
  have h0 : ¬cfg.inputPos = 0 := fun hz => by
    rw [hz] at h₁
    simp at h₁
    omega
  have hL : ¬(cfg.inputPos : ℕ) = input.length + 1 := by omega
  simp only [Cfg.inputSymbol, dif_neg h0, dif_neg hL]
  simp only [show (cfg.inputPos : ℕ) - 1 = p from by omega]

/-- The symbol read by work tape `i`. -/
def Cfg.workTapeSymbols (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) : Option Symbol :=
  cfg.workTapes i (cfg.workTapePos i)

/-- At input position `0`, the blank left of the input, the input head reads blank:
`cfg.inputSymbol = none` (the specification API, user 2026-10-16). -/
theorem Cfg.inputSymbol_of_zero {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.inputPos = 0) :
    cfg.inputSymbol = none := by
  simp [Cfg.inputSymbol, h]

/-- At input position `input.length + 1`, the blank right of the input, the input head reads
blank: `cfg.inputSymbol = none` (the specification API, user 2026-10-16). -/
theorem Cfg.inputSymbol_of_end {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input}
    (h : cfg.inputPos.val = input.length + 1) : cfg.inputSymbol = none := by
  have he : cfg.inputPos = Fin.last (input.length + 1) := Fin.ext h
  simp [Cfg.inputSymbol, he]

/-- Work head `i` reads the cell under it:
`cfg.workTapeSymbols i = cfg.workTapes i (cfg.workTapePos i)`
(the specification API, user 2026-10-16). -/
theorem Cfg.workTapeSymbols_eq (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) :
    cfg.workTapeSymbols i = cfg.workTapes i (cfg.workTapePos i) :=
  rfl

/-- A configuration is halted when it has no state to continue from. -/
abbrev Cfg.Halted (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Prop := cfg.state = none

/-- The initial configuration for a starting state and an input string. -/
@[simp]
def Cfg.init (q₀ : State) (input : List Symbol) : Cfg k Symbol State input :=
  ⟨some q₀, 1, fun _ _ => none, fun _ => 0, []⟩

/-! The specification API (user, 2026-10-16): `Turing.Cfg.init`'s fields as equations
(`Cfg.init_state`, `_inputPos`, `_workTapes`, `_workTapePos`, `_output`), without the
`simp` attribute. -/
attribute [simps (config := { isSimp := false })] Cfg.init

/--
The effect of an action on a configuration: move the input head, write and move on the work tapes,
append the emitted symbol to the output tape, and go to the successor state. This is the part of a
step that does not depend on how the action was chosen.
-/
@[simp]
def Action.apply (action : Action k Symbol State) (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    Cfg k Symbol State input where
  state := action.state
  inputPos := moveInputPos cfg.inputPos action.inputTape
  workTapes i := match (action.workTapes i).1 with
    | none => cfg.workTapes i
    | some s => Function.update (cfg.workTapes i) (cfg.workTapePos i) s
  workTapePos i := cfg.workTapePos i + (action.workTapes i).2
  output := cfg.output ++ action.output.toList

/-! The brief-inventory API, round 3 (user, 2026-10-17; the round-2 gate's finding 1): the fields
of `Turing.Action.apply` as equations, generated by `simps` without the `simp` attribute. The
state is the action's, `(a.apply c).state = a.state`; the input head moves by `moveInputPos`,
`(a.apply c).inputPos = moveInputPos c.inputPos a.inputTape`; each work head moves by its
displacement, `(a.apply c).workTapePos i = c.workTapePos i + (a.workTapes i).2`; the emission is
appended, `(a.apply c).output = c.output ++ a.output.toList`. The work tapes are
`Turing.Action.apply_workTapes` (`Simulation`). -/
attribute [simps (config := { isSimp := false }) state inputPos workTapePos output] Action.apply

/-- A work tape head moves by at most one cell when an action is applied. -/
lemma workTapePos_apply_le (action : Action k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) :
    |(action.apply cfg).workTapePos i - cfg.workTapePos i| ≤ 1 := by
  simp only [Action.apply, add_sub_cancel_left, abs_le, SignType.cast]
  grind

/-- The work tape cells visited by the head of tape `i` along a list of configurations. -/
def visitedOfCfgs (cfgs : List (Cfg k Symbol State input)) (i : Fin k) : Finset ℤ :=
  (cfgs.map (·.workTapePos i)).toFinset

/-- The number of work tape cells touched by the heads along a list of configurations. -/
def spaceUsedOfCfgs (cfgs : List (Cfg k Symbol State input)) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i, (visitedOfCfgs cfgs i).card

end Turing

import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.Abs
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.Int
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.Finset
import Mathlib.Data.Sign.Defs
import Mathlib.Logic.Embedding.Basic
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Configuration

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Deterministic Multi-Tape Turing Machines

Defines deterministic Turing machines with a read-only input tape, `k` work tapes and one
write-only output tape.
The tapes contain symbols from `Option Symbol` for a finite alphabet `Symbol` (where `none` is the
blank symbol).

## Design

The multi-tape Turing machine uses a read-only input tape, `k` work tapes and a write-only output
tape.
The input head can move freely on the input, but any move attempt beyond one cell outside the input
results in no movement.
The transition function can optionally output one symbol, which models the write-only output tape.
Because of these restrictions, we ignore the input and output tapes for space usage of the machine.
The space usage is defined as the total number of cells the work tape heads visited during
execution.

Restricting the movement of the input head is not essential, but useful because it allows
us to easily bound the number of possible configurations of a space-bounded machine. Most textbooks
have this restriction.

Instead of considering the cells _visited_ by the work tape heads, some textbooks
only consider the number of cells that contain a non-blank symbol at some point in the
execution or the number of cells written to. ([AB09] itself splits: Definition 4.1 counts
_visited_ work-tape locations for `SPACE` — the measure used here — but _nonblank_
locations for `NSPACE`.) This allows
work tape heads to freely move at no cost as long as they do not write. It is
important to note that this causes `DSPACE(1)` to include `DSPACE(log log n)`, a class that
contains e.g. the non-regular language `{0^n 1^n | n ∈ ℕ}` (it is accepted by a TM that writes a
single marker on the work tape and then counts the number of symbols by work tape head movement
without writing).
Defining space usage via "cells visited" thus yields the more fine-grained "complexity world" in
which `DSPACE(1)` is exactly the class of regular languages.

This definition is adapted from the one in [Pap94], chapter 2.3 including
the sub-linear space modifications from chapter 2.5 with the following changes:
- We allow Turing machines to choose to not write on a tape. This is equivalent to
  writing the read symbol again but makes it easier to reason about the semantics.
- Our tapes are infinite in both directions instead of just to the right. This definition is
  equivalent (see [AB09], Claim 1.8). It saves us from having to add a "start marker" to
  the alphabet.
- We only have a single halting state. The different ways to halt (accepting, rejecting, etc) can
  be distinguished based on the output.
- The way to prevent the input head to move outside the input is enforced by the interpretation
  and not by a restriction on the transition function. The two definitions are equivalent, but
  not restricting the transition function makes it easier to define a universal machine.

## Main definitions

We define a number of structures and concepts related to multi-tape Turing machine computation:

* `MultiTapeTM`: the TM itself
* `MultiTapeTM.runFrom`: the configuration reached after a given number of execution steps
* `spaceUsed`: the number of work tape cells touched by the heads until a certain step,
    our main space measure
* `ComputesInTimeAndSpace`: a proof that a specific TM computes an output from an input in a certain
    number of steps and using a certain number of tape cells
* `ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace`: a machine computes a function between specified encodings,
    respecting time and space bounds on each actual input.
* `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`: such a machine exists with binary alphabet and finitely many states.
* `ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength`: the specialization to bounds on encoded input length.
* `DecidableInTimeAndSpace`: a proof that a TM decides a language within a certain time
    and space bound.

**The specification API** (user, 2026-10-16): `Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg_eq`,
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.mem_visitedByTapeHead_iff`,
and the split lemmas `visitedByTapeHead_add_subset` and `visitedByTapeHead_step_subset` (moved
here from `Build/StepBlock`, design note O9).

**The brief-inventory API, round 3** (user, 2026-10-17): `Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_some` and
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.outputSymbol_of_some`, a live step and its emission as equations.

**The space measure as a sum:** `Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_eq_sum`, the cells visited on each
work tape, summed over the tapes.

## References

* [Pap94] C. Papadimitriou, *Computational Complexity*, Addison-Wesley, 1994.
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
* [Sip13] M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, 3rd ed., Cengage, 2013.
-/

namespace Turing

variable {k : ℕ} {State Symbol : Type*}

/--
A multi-tape Turing machine with `k` work tapes over the alphabet of `Option Symbol` (where `none`
is the blank tape symbol). Note that it is not required that `Symbol` or `State` are finite
to keep the definition more general. The restriction will be introduced once we start talking about
computability by Turing machines in general.
-/
structure MultiTapeTM (k : ℕ) (Symbol State : Type*) where
  /-- initial state -/
  q₀ : State
  /-- transition function, mapping a state, the current input symbol and a tuple of work head
  symbols to a movement for the input head, actions on the work tape, optionally a symbol to output
  and the successor state -/
  tr (q : State) (input : Option Symbol) (work : Fin k → Option Symbol) :
    Action k Symbol State

namespace MultiTapeTM

variable {input : List Symbol} {tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State}

section Cfg

/-!
## Stepping a Turing Machine

This section defines the step function that lets the machine transition from one configuration to
the next, and the configuration reached after a number of steps. Configurations themselves are
defined in `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Configuration`.
-/

/-- The step function corresponding to a `MultiTapeTM`. -/
def step (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Cfg k Symbol State input :=
  match cfg.state with
  -- in the halting state, we stay at the configuration
  | none => cfg
  | some q => (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).apply cfg

/-- The symbol (optionally) output when executing one step starting from configuration `cfg`. -/
def outputSymbol (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Option Symbol :=
  match cfg.state with
  | none => none
  | some q => (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).output

/-- The initial configuration corresponding to an input string. -/
@[simp]
def initCfg (input : List Symbol) : Cfg k Symbol State input := Cfg.init tm.q₀ input

/-- A machine's initial configuration on `input` is `Cfg.init` at its start state:
`tm.initCfg input = Cfg.init tm.q₀ input` (the specification API, user 2026-10-16). -/
theorem initCfg_eq (input : List Symbol) : tm.initCfg input = Cfg.init tm.q₀ input :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma step_of_halt {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h : cfg.state = none) :
    tm.step cfg = cfg := by
  unfold step
  rw [h]

/-- **A live step applies the chosen action** (the brief-inventory API, round 3; the round-2
gate's finding 1): at a live state `q` one step applies the transition table's action for the
scanned symbols, `cfg.state = some q →`
`tm.step cfg = (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).apply cfg`. -/
theorem step_of_some {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {q : State} (h : cfg.state = some q) :
    tm.step cfg = (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).apply cfg := by
  unfold step
  rw [h]

/-- The configuration reached by running the Turing machine for `t` steps from `cfg`.
If the Turing machine halts, it will stay at the halting configuration. -/
def runFrom (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) : Cfg k Symbol State input := tm.step^[t] cfg

@[simp]
lemma runFrom_zero {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} :
    tm.runFrom cfg 0 = cfg := by
  simp [runFrom]

lemma runFrom_succ_eq_step {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {t : ℕ} :
    tm.runFrom cfg (t + 1) = tm.runFrom (tm.step cfg) t := by
  simp [runFrom, Function.iterate_succ_apply]

lemma runFrom_succ_eq_step' {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {t : ℕ} :
    tm.runFrom cfg (t + 1) = tm.step (tm.runFrom cfg t) := by
  simp [runFrom, Function.iterate_succ_apply']

/-- Running `a + b` steps equals running `b` steps from the configuration reached after `a`. -/
lemma runFrom_add (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (a b : ℕ) :
    tm.runFrom cfg (a + b) = tm.runFrom (tm.runFrom cfg a) b := by
  unfold runFrom
  rw [Nat.add_comm, Function.iterate_add_apply]

/-- The physical input head can move right by at most one cell per step.
**Proof sketch.** Clamping never increases a proposed position. Check the
three movements, then induct over the run, treating halted steps as stationary. -/
lemma timed_input_bound (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    (tm.runFrom cfg t).inputPos.val ≤ cfg.inputPos.val + t := by
  have hm (p : Fin (input.length + 2)) (m : SignType) :
      (moveInputPos p m).val ≤ p.val + 1 := by
    dsimp only [moveInputPos]
    split <;> dsimp <;> cases m <;> simp_all [SignType.cast] <;> omega
  have hstep (d : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
      (tm.step d).inputPos.val ≤ d.inputPos.val + 1 := by
    cases hs : d.state with
    | none => simp only [MultiTapeTM.step, hs]; omega
    | some q =>
      simpa only [MultiTapeTM.step, hs, Action.apply] using
        hm d.inputPos (tm.tr q d.inputSymbol d.workTapeSymbols).inputTape
  induction t with
  | zero => simp
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
    exact (hstep _).trans (by omega)

/-- If a function `f` that maps the configurations of one TM to those of another one commutes with
their `step` function, then it also commutes with their `runFrom` function. -/
lemma runFrom_comm_of_step {k' : ℕ} {State' : Type*} {input input' : List Symbol}
    {tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State} {tm' : MultiTapeTM k' Symbol State'}
    (f : Cfg k Symbol State input → Cfg k' Symbol State' input')
    (hstep : ∀ cfg, tm'.step (f cfg) = f (tm.step cfg))
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (n : ℕ) :
    tm'.runFrom (f cfg) n = f (tm.runFrom cfg n) :=
  (Function.Semiconj.iterate_right (fun c => (hstep c).symm) n cfg).symm

/-- Running from a halting configuration stays at that configuration. -/
@[simp]
lemma runFrom_of_halt (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (h : cfg.state = none) {n : ℕ} :
    tm.runFrom cfg n = cfg :=
  Function.iterate_fixed (step_of_halt h) n

@[simp]
lemma outputSymbol_of_halt {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} (h_halt : cfg.state = none) :
    tm.outputSymbol cfg = none := by
  simp [outputSymbol, h_halt]

/-- **A live step emits the chosen action's symbol** (the brief-inventory API, round 3; the
round-2 gate's finding 1): at a live state `q`, `cfg.state = some q →`
`tm.outputSymbol cfg = (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).output`. -/
theorem outputSymbol_of_some {cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input} {q : State}
    (h : cfg.state = some q) :
    tm.outputSymbol cfg = (tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols).output := by
  unfold outputSymbol
  rw [h]

/-- The work-tape head moves by at most one cell in a single step. -/
lemma workTapePos_step_le (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) (i : Fin k) :
    |(tm.step c).workTapePos i - c.workTapePos i| ≤ 1 := by
  unfold step
  cases hstate : c.state with
  | none => simp
  | some q => exact workTapePos_apply_le _ c i

end Cfg

section Space
/-! Now we define space usage and add some helper lemmas. -/

/-- The set of positions visited by the head of work tape `i` in the computation starting from
configuration `cfg` up to step `t`. -/
def visitedByTapeHead (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : Finset ℤ :=
  (Finset.range (t + 1)).image fun t' => (tm.runFrom cfg t').workTapePos i

/--
The number of work tape cells touched by the head of tape `i` in the computation starting from
configuration `cfg` up to step `t`.
-/
def spaceUsedByTape (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : ℕ :=
  (tm.visitedByTapeHead cfg t i).card

/--
The number of work tape cells touched by a computation starting from configuration
`cfg` up to step `t`.
-/
def spaceUsed (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ i, tm.spaceUsedByTape cfg t i

/-- A zero-tape Turing machine uses zero space. -/
@[simp]
lemma spaceUsed_zero_tapes_eq_zero (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) (h_zero : k = 0) :
    tm.spaceUsed cfg t = 0 := by
  unfold spaceUsed
  subst h_zero
  simp

/-- Each tape's space usage is bounded by the total space used. -/
lemma spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin k) :
    tm.spaceUsedByTape cfg t i ≤ tm.spaceUsed cfg t :=
  Finset.single_le_sum (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ i)

/-- **The space measure as a sum**: the space used up to step `t` is the sum, over the work
tapes, of the number of cells each head visited up to step `t`. -/
theorem spaceUsed_eq_sum (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    tm.spaceUsed cfg t = ∑ i, tm.spaceUsedByTape cfg t i :=
  rfl

/-- **A tape's space as a count**: the space tape `i` uses up to step `t` is the number of cells
its head visited up to step `t`. -/
theorem spaceUsedByTape_eq_card (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin k) :
    tm.spaceUsedByTape cfg t i = (tm.visitedByTapeHead cfg t i).card :=
  rfl

/-- The space used up to step `t` is the space touched by the configurations up to step `t`. -/
lemma spaceUsed_eq_spaceUsedOfCfgs (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) :
    tm.spaceUsed cfg t = spaceUsedOfCfgs ((List.range (t + 1)).map (tm.runFrom cfg)) := by
  unfold spaceUsed spaceUsedByTape spaceUsedOfCfgs
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => congrArg Finset.card ?_
  ext z
  simp [visitedByTapeHead, visitedOfCfgs]

/-- **Membership in a visited set** (the specification API, user 2026-10-16): a cell is visited by
head `i` within `t` steps exactly when the head stands on it at some time `u ≤ t`.

**Proof sketch.** `Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead` is the image of the head positions over
`Finset.range (t + 1)`. -/
theorem mem_visitedByTapeHead_iff (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (p : ℤ) :
    p ∈ tm.visitedByTapeHead cfg t i ↔ ∃ u ≤ t, (tm.runFrom cfg u).workTapePos i = p := by
  simp only [visitedByTapeHead, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_range, Nat.lt_succ_iff]

/-- **Visited cells split at an intermediate time** (moved here from `Build/StepBlock`, design
note O9, with the specification API, user 2026-10-16): the cells visited by head `j` in
`T₁ + T₂` steps from `d` are those visited in the first `T₁` steps, together with those visited
in `T₂` steps from where the run is at time `T₁`.

**Proof sketch.** A visiting time `u ≤ T₁ + T₂` is either at most `T₁`, or `T₁ + v` with
`v ≤ T₂`, and then run additivity identifies the configuration. -/
lemma visitedByTapeHead_add_subset {m : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (M : MultiTapeTM m Bool S) (d : Cfg m Bool S x) (T₁ T₂ : ℕ) (j : Fin m) :
    M.visitedByTapeHead d (T₁ + T₂) j ⊆
      M.visitedByTapeHead d T₁ j ∪ M.visitedByTapeHead (M.runFrom d T₁) T₂ j := by
  intro p hp
  simp only [MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_image,
    Finset.mem_range] at hp ⊢
  obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := hp
  by_cases hle : u ≤ T₁
  · exact Or.inl ⟨u, by omega, rfl⟩
  · refine Or.inr ⟨u - T₁, by omega, ?_⟩
    rw [← MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add]
    congr 2
    omega

/-- **Visited cells after the first step** (moved here from `Build/StepBlock`, with the
specification API): the cells visited in `t` steps from the successor of `c`, and `c`'s own head
cell, are among those visited in `t + 1` steps from `c`.

**Proof sketch.** Shift every visiting time by one; time `0` gives `c`'s cell. -/
lemma visitedByTapeHead_step_subset {m : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (M : MultiTapeTM m Bool S) (c : Cfg m Bool S x) (t : ℕ) (j : Fin m) :
    insert (c.workTapePos j) (M.visitedByTapeHead (M.step c) t j) ⊆
      M.visitedByTapeHead c (t + 1) j := by
  intro p hp
  simp only [MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_image,
    Finset.mem_range] at hp ⊢
  rcases hp with rfl | ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
  · exact ⟨0, by omega, by rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero]⟩
  · exact ⟨v + 1, by omega, by rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]⟩

end Space

open Cfg

/-- One step appends the symbol (optionally) emitted by that step to the output tape. -/
@[simp]
lemma step_output (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (tm.step cfg).output = cfg.output ++ (tm.outputSymbol cfg).toList := by
  unfold step outputSymbol Action.apply
  cases cfg.state <;> simp

/-- The output does not change after the machine has halted. -/
lemma runFrom_output_eq_of_halt
    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input) {τ t : ℕ} (hle : τ ≤ t)
    (hhalt : (tm.runFrom cfg τ).state = none) :
    (tm.runFrom cfg t).output = (tm.runFrom cfg τ).output := by
  conv_lhs => rw [← Nat.sub_add_cancel hle, Nat.add_comm]
  rw [runFrom_add, runFrom_of_halt _ hhalt]

/-- A proof that the Turing machine `tm` on input `input` outputs `output` in at most `t` steps
and uses exactly `s` space.
Note that this does not require the alphabet or state set to be finite. -/
def ComputesInTimeAndSpace
    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (input output : List Symbol)
    (t s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) t).state = none ∧
  (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) t).output = output ∧
  tm.spaceUsed (tm.initCfg input) t = s

/-- A machine computes `f` between the supplied encodings, with bounds depending on the input.
The machine's alphabet and state type need not be finite. -/
def ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace {α β : Type*}
    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (encIn : α ↪ List Symbol) (encOut : β ↪ List Symbol)
    (f : α → β) (t s : α → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, ∃ t' ≤ t a, ∃ s' ≤ s a,
    ComputesInTimeAndSpace tm (encIn a) (encOut (f a)) t' s'

/-- A function is computable within the input-indexed bounds by a machine with binary alphabet
and finitely many states. -/
def ComputableInTimeAndSpace {α β : Type*}
    (f : α → β) (encIn : α ↪ List Bool) (encOut : β ↪ List Bool)
    (t s : α → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (State : Type) (_ : Finite State) (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool State),
    ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace tm encIn encOut f t s

/-- There exists a binary Turing machine with finitely many states that, for every input `a`,
computes `encOut (f a)` from `encIn a` in at most `t (encIn a).length` steps,
using at most `s (encIn a).length` work-tape cells. -/
abbrev ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength {α β : Type*}
    (f : α → β) (encIn : α ↪ List Bool) (encOut : β ↪ List Bool)
    (t s : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut
    (fun a => t (encIn a).length) (fun a => s (encIn a).length)

/-- Resource bounds can be weakened independently on every input. -/
theorem ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace.mono {α β : Type*}
    {tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State} {encIn : α ↪ List Symbol} {encOut : β ↪ List Symbol}
    {f : α → β} {t s t' s' : α → ℕ}
    (h : ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace tm encIn encOut f t s)
    (ht : ∀ a, t a ≤ t' a) (hs : ∀ a, s a ≤ s' a) :
    ComputesFunInTimeAndSpace tm encIn encOut f t' s' := fun a => by
  obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, hc⟩ := h a
  exact ⟨u, hu.trans (ht a), v, hv.trans (hs a), hc⟩

/-- Computability is monotone in the resource bounds. -/
theorem ComputableInTimeAndSpace.mono {α β : Type*}
    {f : α → β} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encOut : β ↪ List Bool} {t s t' s' : α → ℕ}
    (h : ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t s)
    (ht : ∀ a, t a ≤ t' a) (hs : ∀ a, s a ≤ s' a) :
    ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t' s' := by
  obtain ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, htm⟩ := h
  exact ⟨k, State, hfinite, tm, htm.mono ht hs⟩

open Classical in
/-- The Boolean indicator function of a set. -/
noncomputable def indicator {α : Type*} (L : Set α) : α → Bool :=
  fun x => if x ∈ L then true else false

/-- A set is decidable within the given input-indexed bounds when its Boolean indicator is. -/
def DecidableInTimeAndSpace {α : Type*} (L : Set α) (enc : α ↪ List Bool)
    (t s : α → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ComputableInTimeAndSpace (indicator L) enc ⟨fun b => [b], by intro a b h; simpa using h⟩ t s

/-- The Turing machine `tm` halts after exactly `t` steps on input `input`
if its state is `none` at step `t` and non-none at step `t - 1`.
Note that every Turing machine hast to perform at least one step to halt. -/
def haltsAtStep (tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) : Bool :=
  (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) t).state.isNone &&
  !(tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) (t - 1)).state.isNone

/-- If a Turing machine halts, the time step is uniquely determined. -/
lemma halting_step_unique
    {tm : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State}
    {input : List Symbol}
    {t₁ t₂ : ℕ}
    (h_halts₁ : tm.haltsAtStep input t₁)
    (h_halts₂ : tm.haltsAtStep input t₂) :
    t₁ = t₂ := by
  wlog h : t₁ ≤ t₂
  · exact (this h_halts₂ h_halts₁ (Nat.le_of_not_le h)).symm
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le h
  cases d with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ d =>
    have halts₁ : (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) t₁).state = none := by
      simp [haltsAtStep] at h_halts₁
      exact h_halts₁.left
    have halts₂ : (tm.runFrom (tm.initCfg input) (d + t₁)).state ≠ none := by
      grind [haltsAtStep, runFrom]
    refine absurd ?_ halts₂
    rw [Nat.add_comm, runFrom_add, tm.runFrom_of_halt _ halts₁]
    exact halts₁

/-- If a deterministic machine repeats a non-halting configuration, it never halts,
because the sequence between the two configurations will loop forever.
Note that this can be applied to two arbitrary and different time steps `t` and `t + Δ`
using `tm.runFrom_add`. -/
lemma not_halts_of_repeat_nonhalt
    (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
    (h_not_halt : cfg.state ≠ none)
    (t : ℕ)
    (heq : tm.runFrom cfg (t + 1) = cfg) :
    ∀ t', (tm.runFrom cfg t').state ≠ none := by
  intro t'
  -- The configuration will repeat every `t + 1` steps.
  have hloop : ∀ n, tm.runFrom cfg (n * (t + 1)) = cfg := by
    intro n
    unfold runFrom
    rw [Nat.mul_comm, Function.iterate_mul]
    exact Function.iterate_fixed heq n
  by_contra hnh
  -- Assuming the machine halts at step `t'`, it is also halted at step `t' * (t + 1)`
  have h₁ : (tm.runFrom cfg (t' * (t + 1))).state = none := by
    have hle : t' ≤ t' * (t + 1) := by grind
    obtain ⟨tΔ , htΔ⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hle
    rw [htΔ, tm.runFrom_add]
    simp [hnh]
  simp [hloop t', h_not_halt] at h₁

end MultiTapeTM

end Turing
